boundaryDeclaration.storeAuthority: The control store remains the only authority for subscription acceptance, ruleRevision/activationGeneration, deliveries, ack and claim fencing. The plugin-owned EventRuleStore (atomic JSON file) only holds bounded declarative metadata and derived observation/time/wait/intent state; it cannot create, authorize or dispatch a subscription.
boundaryDeclaration.lifecycle: create/update/pause/resume/unsubscribe/list/status expose expectedRevision CAS. Store-level rule changes (types/filter/expiresAt) keep their existing ruleRevision/activationGeneration semantics. Declarative-only changes (condition/notification/time/observation) bump the plugin conditionRevision and explicitly fence the old activation generation via pause+resume, cancelling pending deliveries; the same accepted event cannot become a second match (durable delivery identity excludes activationGeneration).
boundaryDeclaration.onceWait: A one-shot wait is a durable background subscription with once+expiresAt. Waiting consumes no worker slot and calls no model. A claimed delivery is settled by a trusted qualification gate (current Assignment/Goal/pause/budget); denial keeps only the zero-model background reference with an explicit reason. Expiry/cancel close dispatch eligibility and never wake a gate.
boundaryDeclaration.conditions: Conditions are declarative only: white-listed filterable fields, bounded predicates (<=8), operators eq/in/changed/gt/gte/lt/lte/exists, primitive values (in <=16). No callbacks, JS, SQL or regex are representable. A matched condition gates continuation; it does not grant authority or create Task/Goal effects; unaffected conditions remain zero-model.
boundaryDeclaration.timeSource: Canonical occurrence identity = subscriptionId + rule revision (plugin conditionRevision) + scheduled occurrence (kind/revision/scheduledFor), mirrored into the durable event idempotency key. latest-only collapses missed periods to one latest occurrence; skip/grace drops stale ones with a gap. Fresh state/restart establishes a baseline and never replays history; clock rollback, timezone/rule changes and pause/cancel/retire are explicit gaps and never re-fire; duplicate schedule records for one identity accept at most once. One-shot schedules fire once and never after restart. The cooperative pump coalesces ticks, drains in-flight work on close and is gated by runtime pause; it calls no model and occupies no operation slot.
boundaryDeclaration.externalObservation: External changes use an injected read-only observation port with bounded polling (minIntervalMs). Errors/invalid results become visible gaps, never "no change"; unchanged versions produce no events; a changed/newer version publishes one deterministic event. The service never calls a model per tick.
boundaryDeclaration.notifications: Destinations come only from the accepting subscription/request rule; association alone never broadcasts. Every destination gets its own restricted view (metadata + explicitly allowed payload fields only) with a digest. Intent identity is durable (rootEventId+eventId+destination+category) and survives restart/reconnect; delivered/unknown/failed intents are not resent. An unknown send is never retried automatically; only a read-only receipt query can converge it. Causation chains are bounded (default depth 8) and cycles block routing; fan-out and pending intents are bounded with explicit deferred counters.
boundaryDeclaration.unchangedRoles: replyer stays zero-tool; worker/core event tool surfaces and H1/H2a/H2c boundaries are untouched by this slice.

runtimeIntegration.precondition: Construct rule store/lifecycle/reader/time source/pump after `this.events = new EventService(this.store);` and before the background pump starts. Catalog must include H2B_EVENT_TYPES. The observation port and notification effect port are trusted composition (never command JSON). The cooperative pump uses its own timer, no operation slot; allowed() must be false while paused/closed/closing. Close must drain the pump before store close.
runtimeIntegration.failureDegradation: If the observation port is absent, only time schedules run. Time/observation failures are recorded in gaps and snapshot diagnostics, never as "no change". No rule store or no pump leaves the rest of the runtime unaffected; H2b control APIs remain opt-in trusted composition.

gapsAndUntested: runtime.ts integration (catalog + rule store/lifecycle/time pump + diagnostics) is delivered as an exact diff and not live; fixed-host/zero-model probe for H2b is left for Lead.

No real model, embedding, channel, device or real effect endpoint was used: notification Effect and external observation are synthetic doubles; the notification sender adapter (channel/Effect) remains future channel-slice work.

Agent-facing declarative-condition tools are not mounted: installEventTools is not used by runtime today, and the condition/notification API is trusted composition. If desired, a later slice can pass SubscriptionLifecycleService into the generic event tool installation.

IANA timezone database/DST rules are not embedded: daily schedules take an explicit injected zoneOffsetMinutes; a production adapter must supply offsets and report changes. This keeps offline determinism but is not a general tz implementation.
Notification "dedupe survives reconnect" is proven across process/rule-store restart, not against a real platform that may redeliver after reconnect; platform receipt semantics stay unknown.

Causal loop detection uses the bounded visible event history (500); a chain whose ancestors were pruned/not visible is treated as shallow and is not detectable. Cross-runtime echo suppression remains future work.
Budget bounding is structural (maxFanout, maxPendingIntents, chain depth, maxOccurrencesPerTick); monetary/model cost bounding is not part of H2b and no model slot is touched.
DSH host Schedule was deliberately NOT used; a future optional host-schedule adapter may be evaluated separately without becoming the time authority.
